Note::title¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::title() const

Title-Case Every Cell¶

title() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell title-cased: the first letter of every word is put in its title form and the rest of the word is lowercased. Use it for display labels, headings, and proper-noun-ish columns that should read as “Words Look Like This”.

The transform is Unicode-aware — it uses the Unicode default title-case algorithm, so accented Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic words are handled, and a letter with no distinct title form (most of them) simply uppercases. Words are separated by whitespace and by most punctuation; a couple of boundary details are worth knowing and are shown below:

  • A digit followed by a letter starts a fresh word, so "3rd" becomes "3Rd".

  • _ does not start a new word — "snake_case_name" title-cases only its very first letter.

title() changes case only — no trimming, no punctuation removal — and is idempotent. It is shape-preserving and returns a fresh Note. Because some title/lowercase mappings change length, the operation is not byte-length-preserving.

Example 1: A Sentence¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox", "ALL CAPS HERE", "café au lait"}).title())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["The Quick Brown Fox", "All Caps Here", "Café Au Lait"]

ALL CAPS HERE is lowercased and re-title-cased; café keeps its é and gets a capital C.

Example 2: Digit And Underscore Boundaries¶

const pluss::Note n =
    pluss::make_note({"3rd place", "snake_case_name"}).title();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["3Rd Place", "Snake_case_name"]

The letter after the digit in 3rd is title-cased; _ is not a word boundary, so only snake_case_name’s first letter changes.

Example 3: A Scalar¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::make_note("hello world").title()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Hello World"

See Also¶

  • Note::capitalize: uppercase only the first character of the whole cell (ASCII).

  • Note::upper / Note::lower: full-cell case folding.

  • Note::swapcase: invert the case of every ASCII letter.
